One might have the view that moral language is like this: it is meaningful, but not an attempt to describe facts about the world. This view is called emotivism. Emotivism is an attractive position for the moral nihilist, who can then explain why our uses of moral language seem to make sense despite the fact that there are no facts about what is right and wrong.
